sections_en.text: This system is used to protect the emergency diesel areas 1-2. This system is a network of sprinklers on a branch fire water line, always under the pressure of the main fire water network and connected to it through an Alarm check valve. This system does not depend on Heat detectors for its operation, but operates through closed-type water sprinklers that melt when the temperature rises (Auto-fusible link type sprinkler), which activates at 100 degrees Celsius. The system is fitted with an audible alarm device (Sprinkler alarm), which gives a continuous audible alarm when the fire system operates.
The system is also fitted with a Retarding chamber to prevent the Sprinkler alarm from operating when sudden pressure changes occur.

In the event of a fire, the high temperature causes the fire water sprinklers to melt, so the sprinklers open and water flows out of them directly and rushes onto the fire area. The flow of water through the fire valve (Alarm valve) leads to a signal being sent to the control panel and a fire alarm being raised, and also leads to the operation of the audible alarm device.

This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif and reviewed by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed - Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department - the field test was carried out by instrumentation maintenance engineer Raafat Madien, and it was reviewed by the Inspection and Quality Control Sector, Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim - and Chemist Ahmed Abdullah, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan - Head of the Damietta Power Generation Station Sector.

Introduction
This system is used to protect the emergency diesel areas 1-2. This system is a network of sprinklers on a branch fire water line, always under the pressure of the main fire water network and connected to it through an Alarm check valve. This system does not depend on Heat detectors for its operation, but operates through closed-type water sprinklers that melt when the temperature rises (Auto-fusible link type sprinkler), which activates at 100 degrees Celsius. The system is fitted with an audible alarm device (Sprinkler alarm), which gives a continuous audible alarm when the fire system operates.
The system is also fitted with a Retarding chamber to prevent the Sprinkler alarm from operating when sudden pressure changes occur.
How the system works
In the event of a fire, the high temperature causes the fire water sprinklers to melt, so the sprinklers open and water flows out of them directly and rushes onto the fire area. The flow of water through the fire valve (Alarm valve) leads to a signal being sent to the control panel and a fire alarm being raised, and also leads to the operation of the audible alarm device.
This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif and reviewed by Eng.
